clue.text: Wet, tottering Noah, ere 'e dines with wife, got idea Chesterton expounded

definitions.text: Wet, tottering Noah, ere 'e dines with wife, got idea Chesterton expounded

parts.words: Wet, tottering Noah, ere 'e dines with wife, got idea
parts.note: surface reading: a jumble of words that looks like an enormous anagram waiting to be unscrambled
setter's reading: the clue retells a Chesterton poem in which a tipsy Noah, sitting down to dinner with his wife, states his view on liquids

explanation.surface: A drunken Noah, about to dine with his wife, hits on a notion that G. K. Chesterton later set out in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is the refrain of Chesterton's poem 'Wine and Water' from The Flying Inn, where Noah, who has survived the Flood, cares only that no water gets into his wine. 'Wet' hints at the water and 'tottering' at the drink; the letters are not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted refrain is exactly the opinion Chesterton puts into the mouth of the wine-loving Noah as he sits down to dinner.

clue.text: … accepts the situation and a drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrase continuing 27 across, the suicidal setter calmly going along with the idea
second meaning: the stock polite reply when someone offers you a drink

annotation.spelling: I DON'T MIND IF I DO

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue above, someone resigns themselves to their fate and takes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie this to 27 across: the setter 'doing for' himself shrugs and says the phrase, which is also what you say on being offered a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses easy acceptance of whatever is proposed, and it is the customary cheerful reply when offered another glass.

clue.text: One single 26 has a game of cards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one unmarried member of 26 across, an elderly woman who never wed
second meaning: a children's card game where nobody wants to be left holding the odd queen

explanation.surface: An unmarried elderly woman owns a pack of playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is OLD LADIES, so 'one single 26' is an unmarried old lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated term for a spinster, and it also names a simple matching card game played with one queen removed.

clue.text: Bond turned up article on Lincoln and tropical fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another means it comes below it in the grid
in a down clue, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a knot is something that binds or ties
Abraham Lincoln's familiar short name
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: James Bond appears with a newspaper article about Abraham Lincoln and some exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but here it is a tie or knot. The article goes on Lincoln, so after ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonka bean is the fragrant seed pod of a South American tree, used in perfume and cooking, so loosely a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Hoarding shows a church piece with one sharp

parts.note: taken as written
a musical setting of the Mass is a church piece
G major is the key with one sharp, so the piece is written in G

explanation.surface: A billboard displays a church composition containing a single sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' looks like a billboard noun, but it is the verb form. A musical work 'in G' has one sharp in its key signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding means storing up goods or wealth, and gathering things together in quantity is a close synonym.

clue.text: Behavioural questions affected the first gas

indicators.note: something affected has been altered from its natural state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
I is the Roman numeral one, as in first
CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control

explanation.surface: Questions of conduct were influenced by whichever gas came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics is the study of right and wrong conduct, so it is concerned with questions of how people should behave.

clue.text: Bird embracing the French ship launcher

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a female bird, especially a chicken
the French masculine article

explanation.surface: A bird hugs the French ship-launching gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen of Troy had the face that launched a thousand ships, in Marlowe's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe describes Helen of Troy as having the face that launched a thousand ships, as the Greek fleet sailed to recover her.

clue.text: Deep regret about TV detective

parts.note: re means concerning
Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of the television series

explanation.surface: Someone feels deep regret about a television detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is profound guilt and sorrow for a wrong one has done, a strong form of regret.

clue.text: See 1 across
Comic poet has nothing to grind without study

parts.note: zero, nothing

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: to grind one's teeth
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A humorous poet lacks anything to grind and has no study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: the study goes inside the grind word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden Nash was the American writer famous for light, witty verse with outrageous rhymes.

clue.text: Turned out from Plymouth with glands

definitions.note: the fluid named in the phrase that goes with glands

indicators.note: turned suggests being shaken about, so the leftover letters are rearranged
taking something out from a word means those letters are removed

parts.note: the Devon port, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was thrown out of Plymouth with swollen glands.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'out' is itself removed from PLYMOUTH, leaving PLYMH to be rearranged. The definition is loose: the answer is the word that goes with glands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lymph glands, or lymph nodes, filter the clear fluid of the lymphatic system, so the fluid's name pairs naturally with glands.

clue.text: Crown's backing for island and the sun

indicators.note: backing a word means running it backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A crown is supported by an island and the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the island word is reversed; the sun god follows. An ait (or eyot) is a Thames river islet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a type of small crown worn by queens and princesses.

clue.text: Small-time quarrel with centre forwards?

parts.note: a second is a small unit of time
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A petty dispute involving the team's central strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small-time' looks like 'petty', but it is a brief span of time. 'Centre forwards' suggests football; in rugby union the second row are the two forwards in the middle of the scrum, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In a rugby scrum the locks pack down in the middle rank, so these forwards are literally in the centre of the pack.

clue.text: See 1
Stress, in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emphasis laid on a syllable
second meaning: a regional or national way of pronouncing words

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom for 'so to speak', but a manner of speaking is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the emphasis placed on a syllable and a distinctive regional or social pronunciation.

clue.text: A column dividing extremes of country has its attraction

definitions.note: points to the phrase capillary attraction

indicators.note: to divide something is to split it apart by sitting in the middle
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
taken as written
a pillar is an upright column

explanation.surface: A column splitting the remote edges of the countryside has its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the physics term capillary attraction, the pull that draws liquid up a narrow tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Capillary attraction is the force drawing liquid up a fine tube, so the word is the kind of tube or action that has this pull.

clue.text: Destroyer of documents — don''t say a word — increasingly embarrassed

parts.note: the hushing sound telling someone to keep quiet
blushing more and more

explanation.surface: Someone shredding papers is told to keep quiet and blushes ever more deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder is the office machine that cuts paper into strips so confidential papers cannot be read.

clue.text: Butt or object of wag? (1 down has one)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the stub of a smoked cigarette
second meaning: the tail, the part of the animal that it wags

explanation.surface: Is it a cigarette stub or the target of a joker, with an aside about another clue?
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a bonus joke: 1 down finishes with DO, which is 'dog' with its end removed. A dog end is British slang for a cigarette stub.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a discarded cigarette stub, and literally the rear of a dog, where its tail wags.

clue.text: See 1 across
Part of column makes one in part of book

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a book is divided into chapters
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One section of a newspaper column becomes a single entry in a book chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests newspaper writing, but it is an architectural column.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapiter is the architectural term for the capital, the decorated head at the top of a column.

clue.text: See 1 across
Remove the top … of the car''s summer feature

parts.note: the panel in a car roof that opens on sunny days

explanation.surface: Taking the lid off is how a car's sunny-day feature works.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots mean 'Remove the top' does double duty: as the definition, and as the instruction to drop the first letter of the car part.
explanation.definitionFit: To unroof something is to strip away its roof, which is exactly removing the top of a building or vehicle.

clue.text: I'm upset, natch, in view of the very long odds

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the face of a building is the aspect or view it presents

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: slang for naturally, taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone is naturally dismayed, given how unlikely things look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm upset' reads as the speaker's mood, but only 'upset' works, shuffling 'natch'; 'I'm' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic phrase means almost no possibility at all, which is what extremely long odds against something amount to.

clue.text: Composer followed by Sikh, say

parts.note: surface reading: a composer with a Sikh admirer trailing behind him
setter's reading: say the composer's name and then the word for a Sikh aloud, and you hear a children's game of hiding and searching

explanation.surface: A composer is shadowed by a Sikh.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the Austrian composer's name and 'Sikh' sound like the game hide-and-seek.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian classical composer, father of the symphony and string quartet.

clue.text: Try to deceive and don't sail away

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nautical sense of a ship holding position, head to the wind

explanation.walkthrough: In sailing, a vessel that lies to is stopped with its bows facing the wind rather than making way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means telling falsehoods to someone, and in seamanship it means keeping a ship nearly stationary against the wind.

clue.text: Faded-looking small craft losing height

indicators.note: losing something means letters drop out of the word

parts.note: a small open boat
the standard abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A drab little boat is sinking lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingy describes something gloomy and drab, its colour dulled by dirt or age, so faded in appearance.

clue.text: Wives and mothers all do badly on the other side

indicators.note: one part follows on after the other
doing something badly means botching it, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: made other means made different, so this word's letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Wives and mothers everywhere struggle on the far side of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other side' hints at death, fitting DIES, but the letters come from rearranging 'side'. 'My old lady' is slang for one's wife or mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a man's wife or his mum is called his old lady, so the plural covers both.

clue.text: Setter without domestic help being suicidal…

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the compiler with no cleaner, so doing his own housework
second meaning: 'doing for' someone also means killing them, here the speaker himself

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler without a cleaner feels like ending it all.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a cleaner 'does for' a household, and to 'do for' someone is also to kill them; the setter is 'myself'. The dots lead on to 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means cleaning one's own home without a charwoman, and also killing oneself, the setter being the speaker.
